project.title: Culture4All
project.description: Information visualization of access to culture across Italian regions, built on ISTAT and dati.cultura open data, with Corrado Consiglio and Salvatore Di Marzo.
project.introText: Culture for All maps access to culture across Italy: where libraries, archives and museums are, how people use libraries, and how reading habits differ from region to region.

gridImages.caption: Counting libraries rewards big provinces; per inhabitant, the map changes.
Where the cultural institutions are, next to the share of municipalities with no library, by region.
Southern libraries lend a fraction of what northern ones do: loans per public library, 2022.
Where libraries lend less, fewer people read: reading habits by region, 2021.
The findings, each linked back to its chart, and how every number was made.

project.middleText: Built on open data from ISTAT and the Ministry of Culture, the 2026 version is a data story on unequal access to culture: headline figures, a per-capita map from ISTAT's own rate of libraries per 10,000 inhabitants next to the raw counts, ranked bars instead of a pie chart, loans per library, reading habits by region and a loans-versus-reading comparison, with the finding stated and a data table under every chart.
project.conclusionText: Institutions cluster in Lombardy, Veneto, Tuscany and Lazio, cities borrow more than rural areas, and reading habits vary widely, which points to where cultural infrastructure needs investment. Made for Information Visualization (2023/24, University of Bologna) with Corrado Consiglio and Salvatore Di Marzo, who gathered and cleaned the data. I designed the visualisations and built the site with Leaflet, D3.js and Chart.js.
project.highlightCaption: Where you live in Italy decides how much culture you can reach: the opening, with four headline figures.
project.context: Information Visualization, 2023/24, MA Digital Humanities and Digital Knowledge, University of Bologna
project.reworkNote: Culture for All began as a group project with Corrado Consiglio and Salvatore Di Marzo for Information Visualization (2023/24). I reworked it independently in 2026; the version shown here is that rework.

summary.brief: Access to culture in Italy is unequal, but raw counts of libraries and museums mostly show where people live.
summary.role: Data visualisation and web development; the 2026 rework on my own.
summary.method: ISTAT and Ministry of Culture open data, with rates per inhabitant wherever the data allows.
summary.outcome: A data story: one municipality in four has no library, and southern libraries lend a fraction of what northern ones do.
